feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is stated for it. Evidence so far: in iteration 0 (baseline, 60 trials, score 62.3) every run went off track after about one line loss, with max_error 0.061 to 0.063 m and low steering oscillation (0.11 to 0.15). In iteration 1, widening the sensors to ±0.045 m cut oval line losses from 1.05 to 0.55, so sensing reach helps there, but oval progress fell from 0.175 to 0.121 when wheel_track was also narrowed. In iteration 2 (mass 0.6 kg), oval losses fell to 0.35 while s-bend and slalom still showed 1.0 line losses with max_error 0.061 to 0.063 m. In iteration 3 (wheel_track 0.09 m), s-bend and slalom again lost the line once per run (1.0) with max_error 0.0618 to 0.0673 m, and oval progress stayed at 0.121. So mass and track have not cleared the tight bends. I have kept the controller identical to iteration 3 so the wider span is the only change. Read the next race as follows: if s-bend and slalom line losses reach 0 with max_error below about 0.055 m, keep the span and check oval progress. If losses stay at 1 with max_error at or above 0.06 m, the sensor reach is also at its limit, so the remaining gains must come from the controller and the geometry should stay as it is. If oval progress falls below 0.12, return wheel_track to 0.10 m.
requested_changes: If the next race still shows line_loss_events of 1 with max_error at or above 0.06 m on s-bend or slalom: keep the ±0.054 m span and the 0.027 m steps, and keep mass 0.6 kg and wheel_track 0.09 m. Iteration 3 showed the turn-authority levers have been used, so no further geometry change is supported; I will address the rest in the controller.

If line losses reach 0 but oval progress stays near 0.12 or below: keep the geometry as proposed. The shortfall is controller speed, which I will address by raising base_speed, not by narrowing further.

If oval progress falls below 0.12 with the wider span and 0.09 m track: return wheel_track to 0.10 m, the iteration 2 setting, with the ±0.054 m span kept. Iteration 1 showed progress fell when the track was first narrowed, so the track may be costing progress rather than adding turn authority.
